title: The river otters: exercises
subtitle: Five exercises on the text
label: Exercises
review: Written by Claude from the lesson text. Check the English and the answers before using it with learners.

items.q: River otters have thin brown fur.
Otters can close their ears and nose underwater.
Fish are one of the otter's favorite foods.
Otters often rest in hidden places far from the water.
When baby otters are born, their eyes are open.
Playing helps young otters learn useful skills.
What helps an otter find food underwater?
items.why: “Its sensitive whiskers help it find food underwater.”

items.q: What are an otter's safe resting places called?

items.before: They have long bodies, short legs, and thick brown

blocks.title: 4. Open questions
blocks.note: These questions are open. Talk about your answers with your teacher or a classmate.

items.q: Without looking at the text, sum it up in three sentences.
items.model: River otters are playful animals with long bodies and thick brown fur. They are excellent swimmers and use their whiskers to find food, like fish. They rest in dens, care for their pups and love to play.

items.q: How is an otter's body good for swimming?
items.model: Its webbed feet help it paddle, and its strong tail helps it swim and turn. It can close its ears and nose underwater.
In hidden places near the water, like hollow logs, holes in riverbanks or old beaver homes. These places are called dens.

items.q: Why is playing important for young otters?
items.model: Playing helps them learn useful skills, like swimming and catching food.

items.q: What games do you like to play with your friends?

blocks.title: 5. Put in order
blocks.intro: Put the ideas in the order of the text.
items: Otters swim with their webbed feet and strong tail
The otter catches a fish for dinner
Otters rest in hidden places called dens
The pups learn how to swim
